content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "PFS endpoint definition inconsistent between sections",
      "quote": "Progression will be based on an independent radiologic assessment of disease response per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 (RECIST v1.1).",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "2.1.2",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Section 2.1.2 states PFS is based on 'independent radiologic assessment' while Section 3 states 'blinded independent central review (BICR)'. This inconsistency could lead to ambiguity in analysis and potential amendments.",
      "fix": "Harmonize terminology across sections, e.g., use 'blinded independent central review (BICR)' consistently."
    },
    {
      "title": "OS endpoint definition incomplete in Section 2.1.3",
      "quote": "The key secondary endpoints are OS, objective response rate (ORR), patient-reported outcomes (PRO), including change from baseline (cycle 1 day 1) over time to week 12 in disease related symptoms (dyspnea, cough, and chest pain), physical functioning, and health related quality of life (QOL).",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "2.1.3",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The OS definition is not provided in this section; the text jumps to a censoring note without defining OS. This is a critical endpoint and should be fully defined.",
      "fix": "Add a full definition of OS (e.g., time from randomization to death from any cause) in Section 2.1.3."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion 105 requires both platinum and checkpoint inhibitor, potentially overly restrictive",
      "quote": "Prior treatment must include a platinum-based doublet chemotherapy and checkpoint inhibitor for advanced or metastatic disease, either given as one line of therapy or as individual lines of therapy unless the subject has a medical contraindication to one of the required therapies.",
      "page": 58,
      "section": "5.1",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Requiring both platinum-based doublet and checkpoint inhibitor may exclude patients who received only one due to standard practice variations, leading to slow enrollment and potential amendments.",
      "fix": "Consider allowing either platinum-based or checkpoint inhibitor as sufficient, or broaden to 'at least one prior systemic therapy' without specifying both classes."
    },
    {
      "title": "PRO endpoint timepoint limited to Week 12 may miss later treatment effects",
      "quote": "Change from baseline (cycle 1 day 1) over time to week 12 in disease related symptoms (dyspnea, cough, and chest pain), physical functioning, and health related quality of life (QOL).",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "2.1.3",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Assessing PRO only up to Week 12 may not capture longer-term effects, especially if patients remain on treatment beyond 12 weeks. This could limit the interpretability of PRO results.",
      "fix": "Consider extending PRO assessments to later timepoints (e.g., Week 24 or end of treatment) to better evaluate sustained effects."
    },
    {
      "title": "Safety monitoring lacks specific assessments for KRAS inhibitor class",
      "quote": "Subject incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events, treatment-related adverse events, changes in vital signs, and clinical laboratory tests.",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The safety endpoint is generic and does not include specific monitoring for known toxicities of KRAS G12C inhibitors (e.g., hepatotoxicity, gastrointestinal effects, skin toxicity). This may lead to under-reporting of relevant adverse events.",
      "fix": "Add specific safety assessments for KRAS inhibitor class toxicities, such as liver function tests, dermatologic exams, and gastrointestinal symptom monitoring."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion 104 allows prior mutation documentation from another study, potential inconsistency",
      "quote": "Have documentation of KRAS p.G12C mutation confirmed by central testing through the current protocol or have documentation of KRAS p.G12C mutation through Amgen Study 20190294 prior to enrollment.",
      "page": 58,
      "section": "5.1",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Allowing mutation documentation from a different study may introduce variability in testing methods and timing, potentially affecting eligibility consistency.",
      "fix": "Require central testing for all subjects or ensure the prior study used the same validated assay."
    },
    {
      "title": "PFS censoring at start of new anti-cancer therapy may introduce bias",
      "quote": "PFS is censored at the date of last evaluable assessment before or on start of new anti-cancer therapy.",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Censoring PFS at start of new therapy is a treatment policy strategy, but it may overestimate PFS if patients start new therapy due to progression not yet documented. This could bias the treatment effect.",
      "fix": "Consider using a composite strategy or sensitivity analysis that includes progression events after new therapy start."
    },
    {
      "title": "PRO estimand uses 'before or on start of new anti-cancer therapy' but may be ambiguous",
      "quote": "PRO measurements before or on start of new anti-cancer therapy including crossover will be used to estimate treatment effect.",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The phrase 'before or on start' is ambiguous regarding whether measurements on the exact start date are included, and it may not align with the primary estimand strategy for PFS.",
      "fix": "Clarify the handling of PRO measurements on the day of new therapy initiation and ensure consistency with other estimands."
    }
  ]
}
